text:
sam_kim: starting thread for NimbusCorp enterprise commit POC  sales asked for concrete capacity recommendation + defensive autoscale runbook before legal signs the SOW. short Qs below.

marco_garcia: quick profile: expected steady 45 rps (2.7k/min). bursts: up to 500 rps for 1-3 minutes up to 4x/day. avg tokens per request ~350, heavy requests up to 1500. multi-tenant traffic, 60% chat style short-turn, 40% long generation.

rachel_li: model plan: customer wants M-Large quantized (8-bit) for cost. what's our tokens/sec per V100-equivalent for that quant profile? need for rough GPU calc.

pavan_singh: bench: M-Large quantized ~= 9k tokens/s per V100-equivalent under our runtime at 512 seq. safe estimate for planning: 8k tokens/s to include overhead.

marco_garcia: math: steady capacity tokens/s = 45 * 350 = 15_750 t/s -> 15_750 / 8_000 ~ 1.97 -> ~2 GPUs baseline. but bursts need headroom.

sam_kim: sales wants conservative commit for billing and SLA. propose reserved 6 GPUs (3x steady) + burst credits for spikes. feels high, want to hear ops take.

pavan_singh: reserved=6 is conservative but reasonable for SLA and AZ failure tolerance. alternatives: reserve 3 + aggressive burst pool + cross-AZ autoscale, but p95 latency will be less predictable.

rachel_li: can we provide an autoscale policy snippet and a one-line security response about preheat and KV warm? sales will paste straight into the SOW/Questionnaire.

pavan_singh: snippet below (redact internal names):
```
autoscale_policy:
  reserved_gpus: 6                  # committed pool for SLA-backed throughput
  min_gpus: 1                       # keep one warm to avoid cold-start penalties
  burst_credit_tokens: 2000         # tokenized burst budget for transient spikes
  scale_up_condition: p95_latency_ms > 400 or queue_depth > 50
  scale_down_condition: p95_latency_ms < 250 for 10m
  preheat_strategy: kv_seed + prompt-prefetch
  kv_seed_config:
    seed_percentile: 20             # seed top-20% prefixes at preheat
    data_source: synthetic          # no customer PII
```

marco_garcia: short note for sales about tradeoffs: reserved=6 -> predictable billing, lower variable consumption, better p95; reserved=3 + burst -> cheaper commit but expect ~25-40% higher variable GPU-hours and potential 200-500ms p95 penalties during sustained spikes.

sam_kim: security one-liner pls.

pavan_singh: security one-liner: "Preheat/KV-seed jobs use anonymized synthetic prefixes and are executed within the customer's network boundary for Dedicated/Private deployments; no customer PII is transmitted to Redwood-managed preheat processes."

rachel_li: ops blocker: they require AZ spread and a short RTO playbook if an AZ loses capacity. can we document eviction tolerance and fallback?

pavan_singh: yes: reserved pool can be pinned across 3 AZs (preferred) or 2 AZs minimum. with reserved=6 and AZ-spread we can tolerate single-AZ outage for up to ~5 minutes without cross-region autoscale; beyond that we recommend cross-region fallback (manual or automatic depending on contract). add to runbook.

opsbot: infra-bot: preheat template created -> job nimbus-preheat-4420001234, will run KV-seed when commit flips to active. :white_check_mark:

marco_garcia: can someone run a quick cost sim delta: reserve3 vs reserve6 vs on-demand-burst? sales wants 3-line table for the deck.

pavan_singh: i'll run sim with the profile (45 rps steady, 4x/day 500 rps for 120s) and token mix. will post numbers by EOD.

sam_kim: thanks all  action items: (1) pavan run cost sim + post numbers (2) rachel draft the SOW blurb with autoscale snippet and security one-liner (3) marco prep the customer-facing 3-line cost slide. i'll loop back to sales later today. :thumbsup:
